Latent Profiles of HPV Vaccination, Depressive Symptoms, and Metabolic Syndrome Components

Latent Class Analysis of NHANES 2011–2018

Author

Helen Hung (Advisor: Dr. Cohen)

Published

November 9, 2026

Introduction

Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective strategy for preventing new HPV infections and HPV-associated cancers. In the United States, catch-up vaccination is recommended for all persons through age 26 years, whereas vaccination for adults aged 27–45 years is based on shared clinical decision-making; HPV vaccines are not licensed for use after age 45 years (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention 2024; Meites 2019). These boundaries make age particularly relevant when adult vaccination patterns are examined. Nevertheless, HPV-vaccination coverage among U.S. adults remains incomplete and varies across demographic and health-care-access groups (Lewis and Markowitz 2022; Lu 2021). HPV vaccination may therefore reflect not only receipt of a specific cancer-prevention intervention but also broader differences in access to and engagement with preventive care.

Metabolic syndrome (MetS) is a cluster of five cardiometabolic abnormalities: central adiposity, elevated triglycerides, reduced high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, elevated blood pressure, and impaired glucose regulation (Alberti et al. 2009). MetS is common among U.S. adults, increases markedly with age, and is associated with elevated cardiovascular and all-cause mortality risk (Hirode and Wong 2020; Mottillo et al. 2010). Although MetS is conventionally defined by the presence of any three of its five components, a binary diagnosis treats individuals with different constellations of abnormalities as equivalent (Alberti et al. 2009). Retaining the individual components may therefore provide a more informative account of heterogeneity in cardiometabolic risk.

Depressive symptoms add a clinically important mental-health dimension to this heterogeneity. Meta-analytic evidence supports an association between depression and MetS, including evidence that the relationship may be bidirectional and that individual MetS components differ in their associations with depressive symptoms (Kim et al. 2023; Pan et al. 2012). However, research on HPV vaccination, depressive symptoms, and metabolic health has largely developed along separate lines. Evidence directly addressing depressive symptoms in relation to adult HPV-vaccination patterns is limited. The closest related NHANES research evaluated MetS in relation to HPV infection rather than vaccination and represented MetS primarily as an overall diagnosis (Molokwu et al. 2017). Consequently, little is known about whether HPV vaccination, depressive symptoms, and component-specific metabolic abnormalities form distinct patterns within the adult population.

Latent class analysis (LCA) provides a person-centered approach to this question by identifying unobserved subgroups whose members share similar response patterns across multiple indicators. Prior cancer-prevention research has used LCA to show that health behaviors and risk conditions cluster within population subgroups in ways that may be obscured when each factor is examined separately (Kang et al. 2014). Applying LCA to HPV vaccination, depressive symptoms, and the five MetS components may therefore identify multidomain prevention profiles that are not captured by a binary MetS diagnosis or by a series of variable-centered associations.

Accordingly, this study used NHANES 2011–2018 data from U.S. adults aged 20–59 years to identify latent classes defined by HPV vaccine initiation, elevated depressive symptoms, and the five MetS components, and to describe their conditional response probabilities and assigned-class proportions. Age, sex, education, and marital status were summarized descriptively across the assigned classes. The analysis examines patterns of co-occurrence; it does not establish causal pathways or developmental trajectories.

Methods

Descriptive analyses. Participant characteristics were summarized as unweighted counts and percentages and survey-weighted percentages. Weighted percentages were calculated using the adjusted fasting-subsample weights for the combined 2011–2018 cycles. The NHANES masked variance strata and primary sampling units were specified to account for the survey’s stratified, clustered design (Chen et al. 2020; Lumley 2004; National Center for Health Statistics 2018). Survey weights and design variables were used only for the overall descriptive estimates; the latent class models and class summaries were unweighted.

Latent class analysis. Exploratory latent class analysis (LCA) was performed using seven binary indicators: initiation of HPV vaccination, elevated depressive symptoms, elevated waist circumference, elevated blood pressure, elevated fasting glucose, low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and elevated triglycerides. The models estimated class prevalence and class-specific conditional response probabilities under the assumption of local independence of the indicators within classes (Linzer and Lewis 2011; Sinha et al. 2021). One- through five-class models were fitted by maximum likelihood using poLCA in R. Each model was estimated with 10 alternative starts and then re-estimated with 10 repetitions, including the best starting probabilities from the first stage. The number of classes was evaluated using the Bayesian information criterion (BIC), Akaike information criterion (AIC), normalized entropy, class sizes, average posterior classification probabilities, and substantive interpretability; BIC and interpretability were emphasized in selecting a parsimonious solution (Nylund et al. 2007; Weller et al. 2020; Zhou et al. 2023).

Each participant was assigned to the class with the highest posterior probability. Classes were characterized and labeled using the conditional response probabilities of the seven indicators. Local independence was assessed using pairwise Pearson bivariate residuals, calculated by comparing observed indicator-pair frequencies with those implied by the fitted model; values exceeding 3.84 were flagged for further examination rather than treated as a stand-alone model-selection criterion (Oberski 2016).

Class characterization. Class labels summarize the model-estimated response probabilities. Demographic characteristics and the seven indicators were also summarized using unweighted percentages within the assigned classes.

Analysis and Results

Study Design and Data Source

This cross-sectional study used publicly available data from four consecutive cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES): 2011–2012, 2013–2014, 2015–2016, and 2017–2018. NHANES is conducted by the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS) and uses a complex, multistage probability design to produce estimates for the civilian, noninstitutionalized U.S. population (Chen et al. 2020; National Center for Health Statistics 2018). The survey combines household interviews with standardized examinations and laboratory assessments conducted in mobile examination centers.

The cleaned data set included 5,731 adults aged 20–59 years with complete data on the study variables. Because fasting glucose and triglycerides were included as latent-class indicators, the primary analytic sample was restricted to participants with a positive adjusted fasting-subsample weight (wtsaf2yrad > 0), as recommended for analyses that use fasting-subsample measures. This restriction excluded 224 participants and yielded a primary sample of 5,507.

Measures

HPV Vaccination. HPV-vaccination status was derived from the NHANES immunization questionnaire. In the analytic sample of adults aged 20–59 years, this measure recorded whether participants had ever received at least one HPV vaccine dose. The cleaned analytic variable was dichotomized as yes versus no. This measure therefore represents initiation of HPV vaccination rather than completion of the recommended vaccine series (National Center for Health Statistics 2020b; Lewis and Markowitz 2022).

Depressive Symptoms. Depressive symptoms were assessed with the nine-item Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9), which asks about the frequency of depressive symptoms during the preceding two weeks. Items are scored from 0 to 3 and summed to produce a total score ranging from 0 to 27. Consistent with the established validation study and the coding in the analytic data set, high depressive symptoms were defined as a PHQ-9 score of 10 or higher (Kroenke et al. 2001; National Center for Health Statistics 2020c).

Metabolic Syndrome Components. Five binary metabolic syndrome (MetS) indicators were included: elevated waist circumference, elevated triglycerides, low high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, elevated blood pressure, and elevated fasting glucose. These indicators correspond to the harmonized MetS framework, under which MetS is defined by the presence of any three or more of the five components (Alberti et al. 2009).

The reference criteria for the five components are elevated waist circumference (at least 102 cm in men or 88 cm in women when using the U.S. cutoffs); triglycerides of at least 150 mg/dL or relevant treatment; HDL cholesterol below 40 mg/dL in men or 50 mg/dL in women or relevant treatment; systolic blood pressure of at least 130 mm Hg, diastolic blood pressure of at least 85 mm Hg, or antihypertensive treatment; and fasting glucose of at least 100 mg/dL or glucose-lowering treatment (Alberti et al. 2009). The analysis used preconstructed indicators from the cleaned file. The upstream implementation of these thresholds and medication rules still requires verification.

Sociodemographic Characteristics. Age was grouped into 20–26, 27–45, and 46–59 years. These categories correspond to HPV-vaccination policy boundaries: catch-up vaccination is recommended through age 26, shared clinical decision-making applies to some adults aged 27–45 years, and HPV vaccines are not licensed for adults older than 45 years (Meites 2019). Because the data were collected during 2011–2018 and the shared clinical decision-making recommendation was adopted in 2019, these categories were treated as current policy-relevant strata rather than historical eligibility categories (Meites 2019).

Sex/gender was coded as female or male based on the NHANES demographic variable. Educational attainment was collapsed into high school or less versus some college or more. Marital status was categorized as married or living with a partner versus never married or previously married. The underlying variables were obtained from the NHANES demographic files (National Center for Health Statistics 2020a).

Exploratory Data Analysis

The analytic sample was 53.2% female before weighting and 51.8% female after weighting. Survey-weighted percentages were 17.5% for ages 20–26, 45.7% for ages 27–45, and 36.8% for ages 46–59. Some college education or more was reported by 64.2%, and 63.0% were married or partnered.

HPV vaccine initiation was reported by 9.9% in weighted estimates, and 7.2% had elevated depressive symptoms. Elevated waist circumference (53.3%) and fasting glucose (46.4%) were the most common metabolic indicators, followed by low HDL (28.4%), elevated triglycerides (22.5%), and elevated blood pressure (21.8%). See Table 1 for the weighted and unweighted summaries.

Model Selection

The three-class model had the lowest BIC (38,772.32), with AIC 38,620.20 and entropy 0.659. Although four- and five-class solutions had lower AIC, their BIC values were higher and their smallest assigned groups were approximately 5% of the sample. The three-class solution was retained on the basis of BIC, group sizes, and interpretability (see Table 2 and Figure 1). Its entropy was the highest among the fitted multiclass solutions, but does not indicate perfect classification.

Model Diagnostics

Mean posterior membership probabilities for the assigned classes were 0.779, 0.908, and 0.825. Class 1 had the greatest remaining classification uncertainty: its members had an average probability of 0.199 for Class 3. Modal assignments should therefore be treated as uncertain summaries.

Pairwise BVRs ranged from 0.008 to 4.064. HPV vaccine initiation and elevated waist circumference were the only pair above the screening value of 3.84 (BVR = 4.064). Most pairwise associations were reproduced reasonably well, but this remaining association and the extreme HDL probabilities warrant caution. These diagnostics do not establish that local independence holds exactly.

Latent Class Profiles

Modal posterior assignment produced 2,029 participants in Class 1 (36.8%), 1,414 in Class 2 (25.7%), and 2,064 in Class 3 (37.5%). These are unweighted assigned-class proportions. The profiles below are described using the model’s conditional response probabilities, which differ from observed percentages in the assigned groups (Table 5 and Figure 2).

Class 1: Relatively Lower Metabolic Burden

Class 1 had the lowest probabilities of elevated blood pressure (0.036), fasting glucose (0.182), triglycerides (0.048), and depressive symptoms (0.041). Its HPV vaccine initiation probability was comparatively higher (0.170), but vaccination remained uncommon. Elevated waist circumference still had a probability of 0.289, so the class should not be interpreted as free of metabolic abnormalities.

Class 2: Lipid-related and Multicomponent Metabolic Burden

Class 2 had the highest probabilities of low HDL (1.000), elevated waist circumference (0.780), fasting glucose (0.673), and triglycerides (0.511). The probability of elevated depressive symptoms was also highest (0.133), while HPV vaccine initiation was 0.068. The label describes a relative pattern; most members were not estimated to have elevated depressive symptoms.

Class 3: Blood Pressure and Glucose Burden with Low HPV Vaccination

Class 3 had the highest probability of elevated blood pressure (0.388), with prominent elevated fasting glucose (0.633) and waist circumference (0.583). Low HDL had an estimated probability of 0.000, distinguishing this class from Class 2. HPV vaccine initiation was lowest (0.028), and elevated depressive symptoms had a probability of 0.079. The different lipid and blood-pressure patterns make a single low-to-high risk ranking of the classes incomplete.

Descriptive Characteristics of Assigned Classes

Class 1 was younger and more highly educated: 29% were aged 20–26, 61% were female, and 69% reported some college education or more. Class 2 was 58% female, with 46% reporting high school education or less. Class 3 was older and more male-predominant: 50% were aged 46–59 and 58% were male. These are descriptive comparisons of assigned groups, not adjusted associations or tests of demographic predictors.

Conclusion

Main Findings and Interpretation

The analysis identified three interpretable profiles across HPV vaccine initiation, depressive symptoms, and five MetS components. One profile had relatively lower metabolic burden and comparatively higher vaccine initiation. A second combined low HDL with several metabolic abnormalities and a relatively higher probability of depressive symptoms. A third was distinguished by blood pressure and glucose abnormalities, little low HDL, and very low vaccine initiation.

These results describe heterogeneity in how measured health characteristics co-occur. They illustrate why separate metabolic components can provide useful detail when describing health profiles. The analysis does not establish that this representation predicts outcomes better than a binary MetS diagnosis. The depression–MetS literature motivates studying both health domains together (Kim et al. 2023; Pan et al. 2012), while prior cancer-risk LCA provides a precedent for examining patterns across multiple indicators (Kang et al. 2014). Neither line of evidence validates the exact classes estimated here.
